state.label: El Niño Advisory · Very Strong Threshold Crossed
state.detail: El Niño is intensifying toward a very strong event. Weekly Niño 3.4 reached +2.1°C in mid-July — across the +2.0°C very-strong threshold. NOAA holds 81% odds of a very strong peak in Oct–Dec and 97% persistence into early 2027.

narrative: El Niño has crossed the very-strong threshold and continues to intensify. The weekly Niño 3.4 index reached +2.1°C in mid-July — up from +1.7°C in June and +0.5°C in late May — and IRI's mid-July ensemble has 23 of 26 models forecasting a very strong peak (≥+2.0°C) during Oct–Dec, with every model holding El Niño throughout. NOAA's discussion carries an 81% chance of a very strong event at peak and 97% persistence into early spring 2027. The CFSv2 and ECMWF ensembles point beyond +3°C, raising the record-challenging question against 2015–16 (+2.6°C). The event is no longer developing in question or in force — it is now competing for a place among the largest since 1950. The residual uncertainty is whether it beats the 2015–16 record and the exact timing of the autumn–winter maximum. Real-world confirmation is arriving: NOAA raised its below-normal Atlantic hurricane-season odds to 75%, and India's monsoon — after a severe June — is tracking the classic mid-season volatility.
